learningObjective: Distinguish vertical (producer-consumer) fusion, horizontal fusion, and epilogue fusion by their data-flow patterns.

canonicalClaims.claim: Vertical fusion merges producer-consumer ops along a data-flow edge to keep intermediates in registers/SMEM; horizontal fusion merges independent ops sharing launch dimensions to amortize launch/read overhead; epilogue fusion attaches a lightweight pointwise op onto the tail of a heavy compute op (e.g., GEMM/Conv) reusing the accumulator.
conditions: The intermediate tensor is not consumed by any op outside the fused region.
Fused ops have compatible iteration/launch space.
The compute-heavy op provides an epilogue slot (cuBLAS/CUTLASS/TensorIR).
nonImplications: Does not imply fusion is always faster; register pressure, boundary mismatches, or reduced parallelism can reverse it.
Does not imply a single canonical taxonomy across compilers; naming may vary but the data-flow structure is standard.

misconceptions.claim: Vertical fusion means merging operators from different devices into a single kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Cross-device execution is scheduling / placement, not fusion; fusion is a compile-time IR transform.

misconceptions.claim: Horizontal fusion is the same as CSE within a basic block.
misconceptions.whyWrong: CSE removes redundant computations; horizontal fusion merges independent ops sharing launch shape into one kernel — the ops need not be redundant.

misconceptions.claim: Epilogue fusion means merging the backward pass into the forward pass.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Epilogue fusion attaches a pointwise op to the tail of a compute op (e.g., GEMM+bias+GELU); forward-backward merging is a distinct autograd concern.

misconceptions.claim: All three fusion kinds are just names for launching kernels concurrently on separate CUDA streams.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fusion produces a single kernel body; multi-stream concurrency is a runtime scheduling choice, not fusion.

implementationFacts: cuBLAS GEMM epilogue supports bias + activation fusion via cublasLtMatmul.
TorchInductor first fuses pointwise groups, then attaches to reduction/template heads.
TVM Relax uses a fuse-ops pass built on op patterns (injective, reduction, opaque).
performanceScenarios: Vertical fusion of add→relu→mul saves two HBM round-trips of the intermediate tensor.
Epilogue fusion of GEMM+bias+GELU avoids one full read/write of the M×N output tensor.
